title: Offer Acceptance to Autonomy: Accelerated Pathways for New Hires
author: Sofia Martinez
body:
Overview:
This playbook defines an accelerated offering for select new hires and internal transfers that aims to shorten the time from offer acceptance to role autonomy (target: 90 days). It contains eligibility criteria, manager and People Ops responsibilities, a week-by-week manager checklist, feedback cadence, contractor-to-perm conversion guidance, and sample templates. The goal is predictable outcomes: clarity of expectations, measurable ramp metrics, and reduced time-to-impact without sacrificing quality or fairness.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: Individual contributors across Engineering, Product, Customer Success, and Design; excludes executive hires, heavily regulated roles (security/infosec-senior), and roles requiring multi-week facility onboarding.
- Audience: Hiring managers, people-partners, new hire buddy/mentors, hiring coordinators, and L4+ managers approving accelerated pathways.

Why an accelerated pathway?
- Market realities: high demand for senior ICs and internal mobility pressure require faster impact windows.
- Business impact: shorten time-to-first-feature/first-customer-impact to improve velocity and reduce cost per hire.
- Candidate experience: a structured fast path reduces ambiguity for candidates who can onboard quickly.

Eligibility (must meet all):
1) Candidate type: external hire with 5+ years experience in comparable domain OR internal transferee with documented successful performance in previous role.
2) Hiring signal: hiring manager attests readiness with a short rubric (see "Manager Attestation" below).
3) Role readiness: onboarding content, environment access, and at least one low-risk initial project pre-defined in the role requisition.
4) Compensation & compliance: offer banded within target range and background checks complete before start.

Manager Attestation (required at offer stage):
- One-paragraph justification of candidate’s propulsion to autonomy (skills + prior similar context).
- A named buddy/mentor and initial project with success criteria.
- Expected 30/60/90 deliverables.

Target metrics (example SLOs people-ops will monitor):
- Time-to-first-merged-PR (Engineering): 7 days (target), 14 days (max)
- First customer-facing doc/demo (Product/CS): 14 days (target)
- Ramp score (manager-run weekly rubric): achieve >= 3/5 by day 60 and >= 4/5 by day 90
- Access completeness: 95% of required systems provisioned by day 1

Accelerated Pathway Responsibilities:
- Hiring Manager:
  - Submit Manager Attestation at offer stage.
  - Define project and success criteria in job requisition prior to offer.
  - Schedule onboarding calendar for weeks 1–4 before start date.
  - Hold weekly 1:1s focused on ramp metrics (explicit agenda template below).
- People Ops (Talent Partner):
  - Validate eligibility, approve accelerated flag, and add "Accelerated" tag to People Ops dashboard.
  - Coordinate cross-functional access provisioning (IT, security, infra).
  - Assign central onboarding checkpoint at day 7, 30, 60, and 90 to audit and escalate missing items.
- Buddy/Mentor:
  - Hold daily drop-in support first week and three office hours/week until day 30.
  - Run hands-on sessions for codebase/processes.

Manager checklist (accelerated timeline) — week-by-week highlights:
- Pre-start (at offer acceptance):
  1) Finalize Manager Attestation and initial project scope (one paragraph, success metrics).
  2) Provision an onboarding calendar and invite core stakeholders.
  3) Ensure documentation pointers and reading list are ready.
- Week 1: Foundation
  - Day 0–1: Welcome, hardware/access check, team intro, set up dev environment or product accounts.
  - Day 2–5: Pairing sessions, first small task assigned (clear acceptance criteria).
  - End of week 1: 30-minute manager checkpoint (barometer: morale, blockers, access).
- Week 2: Deliverability
  - Assign the first scoped deliverable with clear owner and review gates.
  - Buddy runs three focused walkthroughs (codebase, infra, product flows).
  - Manager sends mid-point note to people-partner confirming progress.
- Week 3–4: Consolidation
  - First deliverable review and merge/ship.
  - 1:1 focused on engineering/process deep dive and growth expectations.
  - Confirm training completion (security, data handling, compliance).
- Weeks 5–8: Expansion
  - Increase ticket complexity; introduce cross-team stakeholders.
  - Manager-run calibrated feedback at day 30 with written summary; people-partner added as reviewer.
- Weeks 9–12: Autonomy push
  - Candidate owns at least one end-to-end workflow or feature.
  - Final ramp review at day 90 documenting outcome: autonomous | needs-extension | transition-out.

Feedback and performance cadence (structured):
1) Weekly short-form ramp note (manager): 6 questions (progress, blockers, risks, confidence, next steps, support needed).
2) 30-day written checkpoint: manager + people-partner + hire signoff on progress against 30-day deliverables.
3) 60-day calibrations: optional peer input for cross-functional roles.
4) 90-day formal ramp review: final decision with one of three outcomes.

90-day outcomes and next steps:
- Autonomous: hire moves to standard performance cycle; manager creates development plan and schedules 1:1 cadence.
- Needs-extension (30 days): defined extension with concrete milestones and weekly scorecards; additional learning resources assigned.
- Transition-out: rare and documented with HR partner; offers internal redeployment or managed offboarding.

Contractor -> Permanent conversion pathway (accelerated variant):
- Eligibility: contractor has >= 6 months tenure and positive mid-contract review.
- Process summary: manager recommends conversion -> people-partner evaluates role budget and banding -> formal offer within 30 days -> conversion start-date aligned to payroll cycle.
- Conversion evaluation components: deliverables, peer feedback, security clearance, and compensation mapping.

Decision points & risk mitigation:
- If access is delayed > 3 business days: initiate critical access escalation to Infrastructure & Security with SLA of 48 hours.
- If early deliverable delayed: manager to de-scope non-critical work and adjust acceptance criteria; escalate to people-partner if recovery not seen in 7 days.
- For high-risk hires (systems with PII/PHI), default to standard 120-day onboarding unless security signs off.

Templates & examples:
- Manager Attestation (one-paragraph):
  "I confirm that Jane Doe has prior product infra experience in a codebase of similar scale, will be paired with Sam Patel as a buddy, and will own the telemetry ingestion POC (success = ingest 100k events/min in staging and owned PR merged). Expected 30/60/90 deliverables attached."

- Weekly ramp note template (email/Confluence blurb):
  "Week X Ramp Note:
   - Progress: 
   - Blockers: 
   - Risks: 
   - Confidence (1-5): 
   - Next steps: 
   - Support needed:"

- Sample onboarding calendar (text table):
  | Day | Focus | Owner | Success criteria |
  |-----|-------|-------|------------------|
  | 0   | Welcome + access | Manager/IT | Accounts provisioned |
  | 2   | Dev environment | Buddy/Infra | First app runs locally |
  | 7   | First small task | Manager | PR opened |
  | 30  | First project review | Manager + PeopleOps | Project accepted |
  | 90  | Ramp review | Manager + PeopleOps | Autonomous / extension decision |

- Example requisition JSON (for hiring coordinators) — add into ATS when flagging accelerated:
  "{ "position": "Senior Backend Engineer", "accelerated_onboarding": true, "initial_project": "telemetry-ingest-poc" }"
Ownership and escalation:
- People Ops: process owner — Sofia Martinez (people-ops).
- Manager: responsible for day-to-day ramping and final recommendation.
- Escalation path: Manager -> People Partner -> Head of People Ops -> Director of the hiring org.

Equity and fairness considerations:
- Accelerated pathway is optional and available to eligible hires; non-accelerated hires receive the standard 120-day onboarding plan.
- All candidates receive consistent scoring rubrics; managers must document rationale to avoid bias.
- People Ops will audit accelerated cases quarterly for demographic parity and outcome variance.

Measurement and reporting (People Ops Dashboard):
- Quarterly KPIs tracked: % hires on accelerated pathway, median time-to-first-merge, % autonomous at day 90, accelerated vs standard attrition at 6 months.
- Review cadence: monthly People Ops dashboard review; quarterly leadership review.

Appendix: quick checklists
- Pre-start checklist (for hiring coordinator): Offer accepted, background completed, Manager Attestation filed, onboarding calendar created, buddy assigned, accelerated tag added to ATS.
- Day 1 checklist (manager): Welcome note, environment verification, 1:1 scheduled, first task assigned, invite to team channel.
